core.title: Speak for Me: Giving LLMs the Situational Awareness to Participate in a Meeting
core.abstract: In online meeting delegation, LLM agents fail to recognize when to speak. With no structured way to track stances, coverage, and floor, they miss the moments where they should contribute. Prompt-only delegates stay silent on 51.4% of the absent participant’s talking opportunities on the AMI corpus. We present CAPA (Collaborative Agent Predictive Architecture), an architecture for online meeting delegation. A Perceiver updates the meeting state from each observed turn. A Predictor forecasts how the conversation will continue. A Controller decides whether to speak and which proposition to surface. A Generator phrases the chosen contribution in the participant’s style. Two judges score the forecast and the action against the next observed turn. A Recalibrator updates the meeting state from those verdicts for future decisions. To evaluate online delegation, we introduce an episode-level protocol that scores whether, when, and what a delegate contributes around the participant’s actual idea units. The protocol’s schema-constrained LLM judges align with human annotations at Cohen’s \kappa = 0.71. On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces the silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5%, doubles credited recovery (26.1 \to 52.2), and keeps hallucination at 0.6%. The failure mode shifts from omission to selection, with each residual near-miss attributable to a specific module of the architecture. Mechanism ablations identify the meeting state as the lever that closes the recognition gap, where raw-context scaling alone does not.
core.summary: 本文研究大语言模型如何代表缺席者参与多人会议，重点解决何时发言以及表达什么观点。作者提出维护显式会议状态的 CAPA 架构，通过感知、行动和再校准持续跟踪对话，并以参与者实际提出的想法单元评估代理。在 137 场 AMI 会议上，CAPA 的未尝试率低于纯文本基线，但未获信用的尝试增多；跨语料测试、模型差异和响应延迟也提示部署仍需谨慎。[P1][P2][P7][P9][P13]

deep_read.problem: 论文关注缺席参与者的在线会议代理：系统不仅要模仿个人表达，还须在多人对话中判断发言机会与应表达的具体观点。纯提示基线容易错过隐含交接，并因缺少对立场、已覆盖内容和发言权的持续跟踪而保持沉默。[P1][P2]
deep_read.method: CAPA 将会议代理建模为部分可观测的序贯决策，维护参与者画像、会议简报及动态状态。Perceiver 更新状态，Controller 先选择动作和命题，Generator 再表达；预测与双评审依据后续观察为状态再校准提供反馈。[P3][P4][P5]
deep_read.innovation: 作者的主要设计是把反馈导向持续会议状态，而非仅改写已生成的话语，并把策略选择与语言实现分离。评估以真实参与者的想法单元为锚，分别考察是否、何时以及贡献了什么，同时限制代理接触未来信息。[P2][P3][P6]
deep_read.findings: 在 137 场 AMI 会议上，CAPA 的宽松召回为 52.2%，纯文本基线为 26.1%；未尝试率分别为 2.5% 和 51.4%，但 CAPA 的未获信用尝试更高。消融显示状态与再校准关联不同表现，作者认为前者影响参与决策，后者细化内容选择。[P7][P8][P15]
deep_read.limitations: 主要评估依赖 AMI 场景会议，ICSI 检查仅含 47 个情节，且性能和安全—覆盖权衡随底层模型变化；GPT-4o 实测响应路径平均 21.14 秒。实时部署还需所有在场者持续明确同意。本批阅读笔记未记录经原页核实的原文件缺项。[P9][P12][P13][P18]
deep_read.connection: 解读：显式状态、干预阈值和可追踪反馈可为智能运维中的告警介入或专家协作提供方法类比；但会议发言与设备故障处置的后果和证据结构不同，现有资料没有验证其在结构设计或可靠性工程中的有效性。[P2][P9]
deep_read.next_steps: 建议先在目标运维流程中定义可观察状态、人工授权边界及干预时机，再构造严格时间隔离的历史回放，分别评估漏报、误干预与建议依据；同时测试延迟和不同模型的稳定性。上述迁移方案是研究建议，并非论文已完成的实验。[P5][P6][P13][P18]

core.title: SocialCritic: Grounding Multi-Agent Dialogue via Advantage-Based Endorsement Suppression
core.abstract: In multi-agent dialogue, a hallucination crosses an operational control boundary when another agent accepts it and downstream decisions inherit the error. We formalize this cross-speaker transition as unsupported endorsement and introduce SocialCritic, a learned receding-horizon controller that ranks and repairs candidate action sequences with separately trained utility, norm, and epistemic advantage critics. Across 692 test episodes spanning LIGHT, DealOrNoDeal, SOTOPIA, and template-family-held-out Persuasion-Conflict over 10 generation seeds, SocialCritic exceeds SAFE-Dialogue by 6.9 points in goal completion and 7.9 points in actionable accuracy while reducing endorsement by 44.9% and norm violations by 42.7%. The public-benchmark aggregate preserves the actionable-accuracy gain (74.9% vs. 66.8%), and trace analysis shows that endorsement falls 77.5% versus 63.5% for initial injection relative to LLM-only. Leave-one-benchmark-out critics retain an actionable-accuracy advantage on every target (minimum 5.2 points), while an H=1 controller without partner rollouts preserves 71% of the full controller’s advantage with 18% lower latency. At the default operating point, batched local scoring requires 1.7 external round trips and 748 ms per turn, enabling propagation-aware simulation, safety evaluation, negotiation, tutoring, moderation, and red-team workflows.
core.summary: 本文研究多智能体对话中无证据主张被其他智能体接受并影响后续决策的问题，将其界定为可干预的背书边界。作者提出滚动时域控制器，利用任务、规范和认知可靠性评论器对候选序列评分，并定向修复风险片段。四个基准的实验显示，相比SAFE-Dialogue，该方法提高可操作准确率并降低背书率，但其效果仍受模拟器接口、自动标注偏差和隐含背书检测能力限制。[P1][P4][P6][P8]

deep_read.problem: 多智能体对话中的风险不只在于某个模型生成无依据主张，还在于其他智能体将其采纳，并据此作出后续行动。作者将注入、跨说话者背书和传播区分为不同事件，研究初始错误进入上下文后仍可干预的控制边界。[P1][P3]
deep_read.method: 控制器生成候选行动序列，由分别训练的任务、规范和认知可靠性评论器进行评分，再对选中序列中的风险片段定向修复并重新评分。默认设置为K=8、H=4、最多修复两次；系统仅执行最佳序列的首个动作，再根据新状态规划。[P2][P4]
deep_read.innovation: 作者将跨说话者采纳定义为轨迹级控制目标，而非仅统计无支持内容的初始生成；同时把任务进展、规范和认知支持分解为独立信号，并将片段级反馈用于执行前修复。其评估还区分有伙伴推演和仅使用当前状态的控制情形。[P3][P4][P11]
deep_read.findings: 在692个测试情节和10个生成种子下，相比SAFE-Dialogue，目标完成率提高6.93个百分点，AA提高7.93个百分点；去除认知评论器后背书率由1.73%升至6.5%。留一基准迁移时，各目标的AA优势为5.2至6.7个百分点。[P5][P6][P15]

完整H=4控制依赖模拟器和伙伴策略接口，隐含背书较难检测，自动化标注可能带来偏差，且实验不是现实用户对话。[P8][P9] 原文件P2图1部分彩色框标签被裁切或遮挡；图注和正文仍说明流程，不影响主要方法结论的识读。[P2]

core.title: SMADE-IE: Sparse Multi-Agent Framework with Evidence-Driven Debate for Zero-Shot Information Extraction
core.abstract: Zero-shot information extraction (IE) with large language models (LLMs) enables adaptation to new schemas and domains without task-specific training. Existing methods mainly follow three paradigms. Monolithic prompting is efficient but prone to missed mentions, boundary errors, and type confusion. Each-type prompting improves type-level focus but may produce overlapping or conflicting predictions, while multi-agent debate can resolve such conflicts at the cost of irrelevant context, redundant interactions, and high token overhead. To address these issues, we propose SMADE-IE, a sparse and evidence-driven multi-agent framework. An Adaptive Mode Selector routes simple inputs to a lightweight Global Extraction Mode and ambiguous inputs to a Type-Centric Extraction Mode based on sample complexity and relevant types. Cross-type conflicts are resolved by an Evidence-Driven Debate module that uses Toulmin-style arguments, external evidence scoring, Beta-based confidence updates, and early stopping. Experiments on nine benchmarks covering NER, RE, and JERE show that MADE-IE improves average Partial F1 over the strongest baselines by 11.37, 3.83, and 14.46 points, respectively. Compared with the multi-agent baseline CrossAgentIE, SMADE-IE reduces token consumption by 85.1% on DocRED and 80.1% on CrossRE, demonstrating substantially higher inference efficiency. Code is available at https://github.com/Cppys/SMADE-IE.
core.summary: 【摘要】论文研究大语言模型在零样本信息抽取中如何兼顾预测质量与推理效率。SMADE-IE依据样本复杂度和相关类型，在全局抽取与类型中心抽取之间自适应选择，并通过证据驱动的多智能体辩论解决跨类型冲突。摘要报告了九个基准上的平均Partial F1提升，以及相对CrossAgentIE的令牌消耗下降；具体实验设置和结果细节仍需查阅全文。[摘要]

core.title_zh: SMADE-IE：面向零样本信息抽取的证据驱动辩论稀疏多智能体框架

article.lead: 零样本信息抽取需要在适应新领域的同时兼顾准确性与推理开销。SMADE-IE 尝试按输入复杂度选择抽取模式，并用证据驱动辩论处理跨类型冲突。

sections.title: 抽取得越细，冲突与开销也可能增加
paragraphs: 大语言模型支持在不进行任务专门训练的情况下，将信息抽取适配到新的模式和领域。但如何组织提示与协作，会影响抽取质量和资源消耗。
摘要指出，整体提示虽然高效，却容易遗漏实体提及、出现边界错误或混淆类型；逐类型提示更聚焦，但不同类型的预测可能重叠或冲突。多智能体辩论有助于解决冲突，却可能引入无关上下文、冗余交互和较高的 token 开销。

sections.title: 按复杂度选择模式，用证据处理冲突
paragraphs: SMADE-IE 是一个稀疏、证据驱动的多智能体框架。其自适应模式选择器依据样本复杂度和相关类型，将简单输入交给轻量的全局抽取模式，将存在歧义的输入交给以类型为中心的抽取模式。
针对跨类型冲突，框架使用证据驱动辩论模块，结合图尔敏式论证、外部证据评分、基于 Beta 的置信度更新和提前停止。摘要没有展开这些环节的具体实现。

sections.title: 三个任务类别的抽取表现与 token 消耗
paragraphs: 摘要报告，在涵盖命名实体识别（NER）、关系抽取（RE）和联合实体关系抽取（JERE）的九个基准上，相比最强基线，SMADE-IE 的平均 Partial F1 分别提高 11.37、3.83 和 14.46 个点。
推理效率方面，与多智能体基线 CrossAgentIE 相比，SMADE-IE 在 DocRED 和 CrossRE 上的 token 消耗分别降低 85.1% 和 80.1%。这些结果对应摘要报告的比较范围，不宜直接外推到所有任务或数据集。

sections.title: 摘要尚不足以判断哪些细节
paragraphs: 摘要未说明各基准的样本规模、数据构成、最强基线的具体身份及各项结果的波动，因此仅凭摘要无法判断比较覆盖范围和结果稳定性。
摘要也未交代模式选择、证据评分和提前停止各自对结果的贡献，或框架在其他领域的验证范围；这些是当前资料无法判断的问题，并不意味着论文没有开展相关分析。

sections.title: 阅读启发：关注路由与证据的作用
paragraphs: 阅读启发：这项工作提示，评估大模型多智能体抽取时，可以同时关注抽取表现、冲突处理和 token 消耗。进一步阅读时，可留意复杂度如何判定、外部证据如何参与评分，以及不同抽取模式下的结果如何比较。

core.title: SkillsVote: Lifecycle Governance of Agent Skills from Collection, Recommendation to Evolution
core.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents generate traces that could become reusable experience, but raw trajectories are noisy, local, and hard to govern. Agent Skills offer a structured artifact for combining procedural guidance, executable resources, and applicability boundaries. Yet open skill ecosystems contain redundant, uneven, environment-sensitive artifacts, and indiscriminate updates can pollute future context. We present SkillsVote, a lifecycle-governance framework for Agent Skills across collection, recommendation, attribution, and evolution. SkillsVote profiles a million-scale open-source corpus for environment requirements, quality, and verifiability, and synthesizes tasks for verifiable skills. Before execution, it performs agentic library search over structured skill folders to expose instructional context. After execution, it decomposes trajectories into skill-linked subtasks, attributes outcomes to skill-guided execution, agent exploration, environment, and result signals, and admits only successful reusable discoveries to evidence-gated updates. Experiments on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and SWE-Bench Pro show that SkillsVote improves agent performance on challenging agentic coding benchmarks. The gains arise from two complementary pathways: online evolution over test-time task streams and offline transfer via frozen libraries built from either historical trajectories or curated open-source skills. We release our code at https://github.com/MemTensor/skills-vote.

core.title: SkillMe: Evolving Agent Skills for Recurring Personal Workflows
core.abstract: Skills help LLM agents reuse procedural knowledge in recurring workflows, but broad transferability alone does not guarantee workflow fit: a reusable skill may be semantically relevant yet fail under local tools, files, formats, and failure modes. We propose SkillMe, a workflow-situated skill evolution framework that adapts agent skills through repeated use in matched workflow recurrences. A Publisher induces and validates an initial skill from a successful execution, while Executors use the skill in agent-native sessions and provide trace-grounded feedback. SkillMe activates the matched skill on demand as workspace files, allowing agents to inspect and adopt guidance progressively without permanently installing it as a local skill. On the 71-task skill-needed subset of PinchBench with OpenClaw, SkillMe improves the overall mean score of all eight Executors over their paired no-skill baselines, with mean gains of +25.7 points. SkillMe thus provides an agent-native path to evolve reusable skills into effective workflow guidance through situated use.

core.title: SkillForge: Learning from Success–Failure Boundaries for Consistent Long-Horizon Agents
core.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often fail from procedural errors such as forgetting constraints, misordering tool calls, or stopping prematurely. Because these slips are unpredictable, the same agent can succeed on one run and fail on an identical task later. The resulting execution trajectories contain rich signals about which procedural choices lead to success or failure, yet existing approaches that extract reusable guidance from agent trajectories either introduce noise through imprecise distillation or depend on external retrievers for deployment. We propose SkillForge, a training-free framework that rethinks both the construction and deployment of procedural guidance: it pairs successful and failed attempts on the same task to identify critical procedural choices, consolidates and filters candidate guidance to remove low-quality entries, and loads relevant guidance on demand at inference time only when the agent’s current context signals its relevance. Across agent benchmarks including \tau^2-Bench and Terminal-Bench, SkillForge improves repeated-run consistency, reducing the consistency gap by up to 37% and lowering total token usage by up to 23.6% compared to baselines, while moderately improving single-trial performance. These results suggest a practical path toward distilling high-quality procedural guidance from past trajectories for more consistent and efficient long-horizon agents.

papers.title: Speak for Me: Giving LLMs the Situational Awareness to Participate in a Meeting
papers.abstract: In online meeting delegation, LLM agents fail to recognize when to speak. With no structured way to track stances, coverage, and floor, they miss the moments where they should contribute. Prompt-only delegates stay silent on 51.4% of the absent participant’s talking opportunities on the AMI corpus. We present CAPA (Collaborative Agent Predictive Architecture), an architecture for online meeting delegation. A Perceiver updates the meeting state from each observed turn. A Predictor forecasts how the conversation will continue. A Controller decides whether to speak and which proposition to surface. A Generator phrases the chosen contribution in the participant’s style. Two judges score the forecast and the action against the next observed turn. A Recalibrator updates the meeting state from those verdicts for future decisions. To evaluate online delegation, we introduce an episode-level protocol that scores whether, when, and what a delegate contributes around the participant’s actual idea units. The protocol’s schema-constrained LLM judges align with human annotations at Cohen’s \kappa = 0.71. On 137 AMI meetings, CAPA reduces the silence rate from 51.4% to 2.5%, doubles credited recovery (26.1 \to 52.2), and keeps hallucination at 0.6%. The failure mode shifts from omission to selection, with each residual near-miss attributable to a specific module of the architecture. Mechanism ablations identify the meeting state as the lever that closes the recognition gap, where raw-context scaling alone does not.

papers.title: SocialCritic: Grounding Multi-Agent Dialogue via Advantage-Based Endorsement Suppression
papers.abstract: In multi-agent dialogue, a hallucination crosses an operational control boundary when another agent accepts it and downstream decisions inherit the error. We formalize this cross-speaker transition as unsupported endorsement and introduce SocialCritic, a learned receding-horizon controller that ranks and repairs candidate action sequences with separately trained utility, norm, and epistemic advantage critics. Across 692 test episodes spanning LIGHT, DealOrNoDeal, SOTOPIA, and template-family-held-out Persuasion-Conflict over 10 generation seeds, SocialCritic exceeds SAFE-Dialogue by 6.9 points in goal completion and 7.9 points in actionable accuracy while reducing endorsement by 44.9% and norm violations by 42.7%. The public-benchmark aggregate preserves the actionable-accuracy gain (74.9% vs. 66.8%), and trace analysis shows that endorsement falls 77.5% versus 63.5% for initial injection relative to LLM-only. Leave-one-benchmark-out critics retain an actionable-accuracy advantage on every target (minimum 5.2 points), while an H=1 controller without partner rollouts preserves 71% of the full controller’s advantage with 18% lower latency. At the default operating point, batched local scoring requires 1.7 external round trips and 748 ms per turn, enabling propagation-aware simulation, safety evaluation, negotiation, tutoring, moderation, and red-team workflows.

papers.title: SMADE-IE: Sparse Multi-Agent Framework with Evidence-Driven Debate for Zero-Shot Information Extraction
papers.abstract: Zero-shot information extraction (IE) with large language models (LLMs) enables adaptation to new schemas and domains without task-specific training. Existing methods mainly follow three paradigms. Monolithic prompting is efficient but prone to missed mentions, boundary errors, and type confusion. Each-type prompting improves type-level focus but may produce overlapping or conflicting predictions, while multi-agent debate can resolve such conflicts at the cost of irrelevant context, redundant interactions, and high token overhead. To address these issues, we propose SMADE-IE, a sparse and evidence-driven multi-agent framework. An Adaptive Mode Selector routes simple inputs to a lightweight Global Extraction Mode and ambiguous inputs to a Type-Centric Extraction Mode based on sample complexity and relevant types. Cross-type conflicts are resolved by an Evidence-Driven Debate module that uses Toulmin-style arguments, external evidence scoring, Beta-based confidence updates, and early stopping. Experiments on nine benchmarks covering NER, RE, and JERE show that MADE-IE improves average Partial F1 over the strongest baselines by 11.37, 3.83, and 14.46 points, respectively. Compared with the multi-agent baseline CrossAgentIE, SMADE-IE reduces token consumption by 85.1% on DocRED and 80.1% on CrossRE, demonstrating substantially higher inference efficiency. Code is available at https://github.com/Cppys/SMADE-IE.

papers.title_zh: SMADE-IE：面向零样本信息抽取的证据驱动辩论稀疏多智能体框架

article.lead: 零样本信息抽取需要在适应新领域的同时兼顾准确性与推理开销。SMADE-IE 尝试按输入复杂度选择抽取模式，并用证据驱动辩论处理跨类型冲突。

sections.title: 抽取得越细，冲突与开销也可能增加
paragraphs: 大语言模型支持在不进行任务专门训练的情况下，将信息抽取适配到新的模式和领域。但如何组织提示与协作，会影响抽取质量和资源消耗。
摘要指出，整体提示虽然高效，却容易遗漏实体提及、出现边界错误或混淆类型；逐类型提示更聚焦，但不同类型的预测可能重叠或冲突。多智能体辩论有助于解决冲突，却可能引入无关上下文、冗余交互和较高的 token 开销。

sections.title: 按复杂度选择模式，用证据处理冲突
paragraphs: SMADE-IE 是一个稀疏、证据驱动的多智能体框架。其自适应模式选择器依据样本复杂度和相关类型，将简单输入交给轻量的全局抽取模式，将存在歧义的输入交给以类型为中心的抽取模式。
针对跨类型冲突，框架使用证据驱动辩论模块，结合图尔敏式论证、外部证据评分、基于 Beta 的置信度更新和提前停止。摘要没有展开这些环节的具体实现。

sections.title: 三个任务类别的抽取表现与 token 消耗
paragraphs: 摘要报告，在涵盖命名实体识别（NER）、关系抽取（RE）和联合实体关系抽取（JERE）的九个基准上，相比最强基线，SMADE-IE 的平均 Partial F1 分别提高 11.37、3.83 和 14.46 个点。
推理效率方面，与多智能体基线 CrossAgentIE 相比，SMADE-IE 在 DocRED 和 CrossRE 上的 token 消耗分别降低 85.1% 和 80.1%。这些结果对应摘要报告的比较范围，不宜直接外推到所有任务或数据集。

sections.title: 摘要尚不足以判断哪些细节
paragraphs: 摘要未说明各基准的样本规模、数据构成、最强基线的具体身份及各项结果的波动，因此仅凭摘要无法判断比较覆盖范围和结果稳定性。
摘要也未交代模式选择、证据评分和提前停止各自对结果的贡献，或框架在其他领域的验证范围；这些是当前资料无法判断的问题，并不意味着论文没有开展相关分析。

sections.title: 阅读启发：关注路由与证据的作用
paragraphs: 阅读启发：这项工作提示，评估大模型多智能体抽取时，可以同时关注抽取表现、冲突处理和 token 消耗。进一步阅读时，可留意复杂度如何判定、外部证据如何参与评分，以及不同抽取模式下的结果如何比较。

papers.title: SkillsVote: Lifecycle Governance of Agent Skills from Collection, Recommendation to Evolution
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents generate traces that could become reusable experience, but raw trajectories are noisy, local, and hard to govern. Agent Skills offer a structured artifact for combining procedural guidance, executable resources, and applicability boundaries. Yet open skill ecosystems contain redundant, uneven, environment-sensitive artifacts, and indiscriminate updates can pollute future context. We present SkillsVote, a lifecycle-governance framework for Agent Skills across collection, recommendation, attribution, and evolution. SkillsVote profiles a million-scale open-source corpus for environment requirements, quality, and verifiability, and synthesizes tasks for verifiable skills. Before execution, it performs agentic library search over structured skill folders to expose instructional context. After execution, it decomposes trajectories into skill-linked subtasks, attributes outcomes to skill-guided execution, agent exploration, environment, and result signals, and admits only successful reusable discoveries to evidence-gated updates. Experiments on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and SWE-Bench Pro show that SkillsVote improves agent performance on challenging agentic coding benchmarks. The gains arise from two complementary pathways: online evolution over test-time task streams and offline transfer via frozen libraries built from either historical trajectories or curated open-source skills. We release our code at https://github.com/MemTensor/skills-vote.

papers.title: SkillMe: Evolving Agent Skills for Recurring Personal Workflows
papers.abstract: Skills help LLM agents reuse procedural knowledge in recurring workflows, but broad transferability alone does not guarantee workflow fit: a reusable skill may be semantically relevant yet fail under local tools, files, formats, and failure modes. We propose SkillMe, a workflow-situated skill evolution framework that adapts agent skills through repeated use in matched workflow recurrences. A Publisher induces and validates an initial skill from a successful execution, while Executors use the skill in agent-native sessions and provide trace-grounded feedback. SkillMe activates the matched skill on demand as workspace files, allowing agents to inspect and adopt guidance progressively without permanently installing it as a local skill. On the 71-task skill-needed subset of PinchBench with OpenClaw, SkillMe improves the overall mean score of all eight Executors over their paired no-skill baselines, with mean gains of +25.7 points. Comparisons show that evolved task-scoped skills are more stable than static skills and more reliable than broadly reusable skills. SkillMe thus provides an agent-native path to evolve reusable skills into effective workflow guidance through situated use.

papers.title: SkillForge: Learning from Success–Failure Boundaries for Consistent Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon LLM agents often fail from procedural errors such as forgetting constraints, misordering tool calls, or stopping prematurely. Because these slips are unpredictable, the same agent can succeed on one run and fail on an identical task later. The resulting execution trajectories contain rich signals about which procedural choices lead to success or failure, yet existing approaches that extract reusable guidance from agent trajectories either introduce noise through imprecise distillation or depend on external retrievers for deployment. We propose SkillForge, a training-free framework that rethinks both the construction and deployment of procedural guidance: it pairs successful and failed attempts on the same task to identify critical procedural choices, consolidates and filters candidate guidance to remove low-quality entries, and loads relevant guidance on demand at inference time only when the agent’s current context signals its relevance. Across agent benchmarks including \tau^2-Bench and Terminal-Bench, SkillForge improves repeated-run consistency, reducing the consistency gap by up to 37% and lowering total token usage by up to 23.6% compared to baselines, while moderately improving single-trial performance. These results suggest a practical path toward distilling high-quality procedural guidance from past trajectories for more consistent and efficient long-horizon agents.
